project_title: The Classified Seconds That Almost Ended Humanity: 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident

scenes.audio_text: At 12:15 AM on September 26, 1983, a red siren illuminated a top-secret Soviet bunker outside Moscow. The radar screens confirmed what every officer dreaded: five American nuclear warheads were already in the air.

Soviet protocol gave Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov exactly twenty minutes to authorize a retaliatory strike that would wipe three hundred million people off the face of the Earth. (pausa: 2s) The machine demanded retaliation. The satellite algorithms swore the missiles were real.

He had a direct line to the Kremlin. His finger hovered over the confirmation switch. But instead of following orders... (pausa: 2s) Petrov decided to trust a hunch. If the United States was going to start World War Three... why send only five missiles?
